subject: Career
title: Sections That Don't Belong
description: Learn Sections That Don't Belong in one minute.

hook.text: 'References available upon request.' Every recruiter already knows that. It wastes a line.

buildup.text: Objective statements, headshot photos, and full addresses are outdated relics.

discovery.text: Each dead section steals space from something that could prove your value.

twist.text: In some countries photos are expected. Context matters — research the local norm.

climax.text: The test: does this section help a recruiter say yes? If not, delete it.

punchline.text: Every line is real estate. Don't waste it.

quiz.question: Which resume section is considered outdated in most Western markets?

details.summary: Several once-standard resume sections actively harm your candidacy in modern hiring. Objective statements, references sections, personal information like age and marital status, and irrelevant hobbies waste space and can introduce unconscious bias.
details.whyItMatters: Every line of resume space is valuable. Outdated sections consume space that could be used for compelling accomplishments while revealing information that can trigger bias.
takeaways: Remove objective statements and replace with a professional summary
Never include references or the phrase 'references available upon request'
Omit personal details like age, marital status, and photo in most markets

faq.question: Why are objective statements considered outdated on modern resumes?
faq.answer: Objective statements tell the employer what you want rather than what you offer. A professional summary that highlights your value and key qualifications is more compelling because it addresses the employer's needs. The shift from 'I want' to 'I offer' dramatically improves first impressions.

faq.question: Should you ever include hobbies or personal interests on your resume?
faq.answer: Only if they are directly relevant to the role or company culture and you have space after including all important qualifications. For very senior roles, hobbies add a human touch. For most applications, the space is better used for additional accomplishments or skills.
